# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

CHANGELOG has an `## Unreleased` section with detailed entries per gh-XXXX. The repo convention clearly adds an entry per change. I'll add one for gh-1589 (both the fa seal and the adapter exit guarantee).

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

CHANGELOG has an `## Unreleased` section with detailed entries per gh-XXXX. The repo convention clearly adds an entry per change. I'll add one for gh-1589 (both the fa seal and the adapter exit guarantee).

Now the AGENTS.md update — find the headless drain paragraph (around line 247) and add a sentence about the close boundary. Let me view the exact context to edit.

2. `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice` — I kept `_tuiController?.sendOutput` before the guard; only `_startRun` is fenced. During drain, isBusy leg steers. Post-fence idle: message echo'd but no run — hmm, the echo would show a notice that's dropped. Edge-case: liveness notices can't fire post-fence (steering happens inside drain rounds only). Leave.

3. The `runHeadless` catch: I set the fence before printing the error. ✓

4. Subtle issue — `_finishHeadlessDrain` sets the fence, THEN `if (isBusy) { await _settled; await _afterRun(); }`. During that await, `_onShellJobSettled` for ANOTHER job settling is fenced → bookkeeping only. Good — that's E1's contract. But WAIT: is there a case during a NORMAL drain where a settle legitimately starts a reaction run and the drain expects to await it? Yes — during rounds (fence not yet up). The fence only goes up at wrap-up. But consider: settle lands in round N's wake → `_startRun` starts → round loop continues → `_headlessDrainAction` still drain → round N awaits... the run is awaited in `if (isBusy)`. Fine — unchanged behavior.

5. What about the `waitForJobs` (visible-waiting) mode: after the drain, `waitForJobsOrSummarize(waitForJobs: true)` waits for timers/jobs. Settles arriving during THAT wait: fence is NOT yet up (set only in `_finishHeadlessDrain`... wait — no: `_finishHeadlessDrain` runs BEFORE `waitForJobsOrSummarize` in the else branch:
```dart
await _awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs();   // ends with _finishHeadlessDrain → fence up
await _waiting.waitForJobsOrSummarize(waitForJobs: waitForJobs);
```
So in waitForJobs mode the fence is already up when waiters run — settles during the waiter stretch do bookkeeping only, and `_waiting.jobSettled` still processes the waiting-row leave. Hmm — is that a behavior change for the waitForJobs mode? Previously a settle during the waiter stretch would `_startRun` a reaction turn (visible waiting). Now it won't. Is that OK? AC2's language: "a background-shell settle arriving after the final answer's drain runs board bookkeeping only" — the drain INCLUDES the wrap-up; the waiter stretch is after it. The fence semantics: the run is exiting; new runs during the waiter stretch would extend the trial indefinitely (that's what gh-1455's abort path explicitly avoids). For waitForJobs=true the user opted into waiting for JOBS, not for infinite reaction chains. I judge the fence during the waiter stretch correct per AC1/AC2 (any terminal path seals). Documented in the response.

6. Check the `_waiting.jobSettled` call stays OUTSIDE the fence — yes: fence check is after it in `_onShellJobSettled`.

arguments.content:
### What changed

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). The headless `finally` and the REPL teardown seal as the LAST session action — same implementation, same close order: drain → usage fold → seal → exit (REG-2).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).
- Honest drains stay legal: assertions pin records to process exit, not the final-answer timestamp (E7/REG-1 guard).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v   # +6 AgentPhaseExitGuaranteeTest (AC4/AC7/IT-3/IT-5)
```

Full suites: `dart test` (Dart CI) and the bench-tests job cover both; the new tests embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (file byte-stable after exit; no record timestamped after exit).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain rounds ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — writers drop + warn once per class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settles after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal state, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel/timeout] --> K[kill fa: SIGTERM → SIGKILL → reap bounded]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

Second tier left as follow-up (per the ticket's tiering): SIGTERM graceful-seal path, tb-twin adapter (`bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`), and the standalone REG-1/REG-2 CI jobs — the invariants themselves are enforced and tested here.

blocks.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,

{"content":"### What changed

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). The headless `finally` and the REPL teardown seal as the LAST session action — same implementation, same close order: drain → usage fold → seal → exit (REG-2).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).
- Honest drains stay legal: assertions pin records to process exit, not the final-answer timestamp (E7/REG-1 guard).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v   # +6 AgentPhaseExitGuaranteeTest (AC4/AC7/IT-3/IT-5)
```

Full suites: `dart test` (Dart CI) and the bench-tests job cover both; the new tests embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (file byte-stable after exit; no record timestamped after exit).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain rounds ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — writers drop + warn once per class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settles after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal state, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel/timeout] --> K[kill fa: SIGTERM → SIGKILL → reap bounded]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

Second tier left as follow-up (per the ticket's tiering): SIGTERM graceful-seal path, tb-twin adapter (`bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`), and the standalone REG-1/REG-2 CI jobs — the invariants themselves are enforced and tested here.

# Changelog

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).
- Honest drains stay legal: assertions pin records to process exit, not the final-answer timestamp (E7/REG-1 guard).

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

CHANGELOG has an `## Unreleased` section with detailed entries per gh-XXXX. The repo convention clearly adds an entry per change. I'll add one for gh-1589 (both the fa seal and the adapter exit guarantee).

Now the AGENTS.md update — find the headless drain paragraph (around line 247) and add a sentence about the close boundary. Let me view the exact context to edit.

Now let me review my full diff while the test suite runs. Check `git status` and `git diff --stat`, and review the changes carefully for issues:

1. One thing I want to double-check: the `_onShellJobSettled` fence also gates the TUI echo — wait, no: I placed the fence check AFTER the `io.writeln('[bash] ...')` but the `_tuiController?.sendOutput('$message\n')` echo happens after the fence check (returns before composing). ✓

2. `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice` — I kept `_tuiController?.sendOutput` before the guard; only `_startRun` is fenced. During drain, isBusy leg steers. Post-fence idle: message echo'd but no run — hmm, the echo would show a notice that's dropped. Edge-case: liveness notices can't fire post-fence (steering happens inside drain rounds only). Leave.

3. The `runHeadless` catch: I set the fence before printing the error. ✓

4. Subtle issue — `_finishHeadlessDrain` sets the fence, THEN `if (isBusy) { await _settled; await _afterRun(); }`. During that await, `_onShellJobSettled` for ANOTHER job settling is fenced → bookkeeping only. Good — that's E1's contract. But WAIT: is there a case during a NORMAL drain where a settle legitimately starts a reaction run and the drain expects to await it? Yes — during rounds (fence not yet up). The fence only goes up at wrap-up. But consider: settle lands in round N's wake → `_startRun` starts → round loop continues → `_headlessDrainAction` still drain → round N awaits... the run is awaited in `if (isBusy)`. Fine — unchanged behavior.

5. What about the `waitForJobs` (visible-waiting) mode: after the drain, `waitForJobsOrSummarize(waitForJobs: true)` waits for timers/jobs. Settles arriving during THAT wait: fence is NOT yet up (set only in `_finishHeadlessDrain`... wait — no: `_finishHeadlessDrain` runs BEFORE `waitForJobsOrSummarize` in the else branch:
```dart
await _awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs();   // ends with _finishHeadlessDrain → fence up
await _waiting.waitForJobsOrSummarize(waitForJobs: waitForJobs);
```

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

CHANGELOG has an `## Unreleased` section with detailed entries per gh-XXXX. The repo convention clearly adds an entry per change. I'll add one for gh-1589 (both the fa seal and the adapter exit guarantee).

Now the AGENTS.md update — find the headless drain paragraph (around line 247) and add a sentence about the close boundary. Let me view the exact context to edit.

Now let me review my full diff while the test suite runs. Check `git status` and `git diff --stat`, and review the changes carefully for issues:

1. One thing I want to double-check: the `_onShellJobSettled` fence also gates the TUI echo — wait, no: I placed the fence check AFTER the `io.writeln('[bash] ...')` but the `_tuiController?.sendOutput('$message\n')` echo happens after the fence check (returns before composing). ✓

2. `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice` — I kept `_tuiController?.sendOutput` before the guard; only `_startRun` is fenced. During drain, isBusy leg steers. Post-fence idle: message echo'd but no run — hmm, the echo would show a notice that's dropped. Edge-case: liveness notices can't fire post-fence (steering happens inside drain rounds only). Leave.

3. The `runHeadless` catch: I set the fence before printing the error. ✓

4. Subtle issue — `_finishHeadlessDrain` sets the fence, THEN `if (isBusy) { await _settled; await _afterRun(); }`. During that await, `_onShellJobSettled` for ANOTHER job settling is fenced → bookkeeping only. Good — that's E1's contract. But WAIT: is there a case during a NORMAL drain where a settle legitimately starts a reaction run and the drain expects to await it? Yes — during rounds (fence not yet up). The fence only goes up at wrap-up. But consider: settle lands in round N's wake → `_startRun` starts → round loop continues → `_headlessDrainAction` still drain → round N awaits... the run is awaited in `if (isBusy)`. Fine — unchanged behavior.

5. What about the `waitForJobs` (visible-waiting) mode: after the drain, `waitForJobsOrSummarize(waitForJobs: true)` waits for timers/jobs. Settles arriving during THAT wait: fence is NOT yet up (set only in `_finishHeadlessDrain`... wait — no: `_finishHeadlessDrain` runs BEFORE `waitForJobsOrSummarize` in the else branch:
```dart
await _awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs();   // ends with _finishHeadlessDrain → fence up
await _waiting.waitForJobsOrSummarize(waitForJobs: waitForJobs);
```
So in waitForJobs mode the fence is already up when waiters run — settles during the waiter stretch do bookkeeping only, and `_waiting.jobSettled` still processes the waiting-row leave. Hmm — is that a behavior change for the waitForJobs mode? Previously a settle during the waiter stretch would `_startRun` a reaction turn (visible waiting). Now it won't. Is that OK? AC2's language: "a background-shell settle arriving after the final answer's drain runs board bookkeeping only" — the drain INCLUDES the wrap-up; the waiter stretch is after it. The fence semantics: the run is exiting; new runs during the waiter stretch would extend the trial indefinitely (that's what gh-1455's abort path explicitly avoids). For waitForJobs=true the user opted into waiting for JOBS, not for infinite reaction chains. I judge the fence during the waiter stretch correct per AC1/AC2 (any terminal path seals). Documented in the response.

6. Check the `_waiting.jobSettled` call stays OUTSIDE the fence — yes: fence check is after it in `_onShellJobSettled`.

+    async def _kill_fa(self, environment, *, force: bool = False) -> bool:
+        """Best-effort SIGTERM (or SIGKILL with `force`) of the fa process.
+
+        Never raises — a failed kill is the escalation path's input, and
+        its failure must never replace the caller's own outcome (the

+        """
+        flag = "-9 " if force else ""

+                timeout_sec=15,
+            )

+        except Exception:

+        """Whether fa has exited, checked with ONE bounded server-side
+        poll loop (`pgrep` once a second for [timeout] seconds). A transport
+        error conservatively reports "alive" — the caller escalates.

+                    f"pgrep -f '{_AGENT_KILL_PATTERN}' >/dev/null 2>&1 "

+            return result.return_code == 0
+        except Exception:

+            try:
+                await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(exec_task), timeout=timeout)
+                return True
+            except asyncio.CancelledError:

+            except Exception:

+        return await self._fa_process_gone(environment, timeout)

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

Post-fence idle: message echo'd but no run — hmm, the echo would show a notice that's dropped. Edge-case: liveness notices can't fire post-fence (steering happens inside drain rounds only). Leave.

3. The `runHeadless` catch: I set the fence before printing the error. ✓

But consider: settle lands in round N's wake → `_startRun` starts → round loop continues → `_headlessDrainAction` still drain → round N awaits... the run is awaited in `if (isBusy)`. The fence semantics: the run is exiting; new runs during the waiter stretch would extend the trial indefinitely (that's what gh-1455's abort path explicitly avoids). # Changelog

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

# Changelog

on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

+    async def _kill_fa(self, environment, *, force: bool = False) -> bool:
+        """Best-effort SIGTERM (or SIGKILL with `force`) of the fa process.
+
+        Never raises — a failed kill is the escalation path's input, and
+        its failure must never replace the caller's own outcome (the
+        gh-1556 AC1 rule).
+        """
+        flag = "-9 " if force else ""

+                timeout_sec=15,
+            )
+            return True
+        except Exception:
+            return False
+
+    async def _fa_process_gone(self, environment, timeout: float) -> bool:
+        """Whether fa has exited, checked with ONE bounded server-side
+        poll loop (`pgrep` once a second for [timeout] seconds). A transport
+        error conservatively reports "alive" — the caller escalates.
+        """
+        try:

+            )

+        except Exception:

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

CHANGELOG has an `## Unreleased` section with detailed entries per gh-XXXX. The repo convention clearly adds an entry per change. I'll add one for gh-1589 (both the fa seal and the adapter exit guarantee).

Now the AGENTS.md update — find the headless drain paragraph (around line 247) and add a sentence about the close boundary. Let me view the exact context to edit.

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). - fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). - Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

CHANGELOG has an `## Unreleased` section with detailed entries per gh-XXXX. The repo convention clearly adds an entry per change. I'll add one for gh-1589 (both the fa seal and the adapter exit guarantee).

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

{"content":"### What changed

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). The headless `finally` and the REPL teardown seal as the LAST session action — same implementation, same close order: drain → usage fold → seal → exit (REG-2).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

# Changelog

on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

{"content":"### What changed

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). The headless `finally` and the REPL teardown seal as the LAST session action — same implementation, same close order: drain → usage fold → seal → exit (REG-2).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).
- Honest drains stay legal: assertions pin records to process exit, not the final-answer timestamp (E7/REG-1 guard).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v   # +6 AgentPhaseExitGuaranteeTest (AC4/AC7/IT-3/IT-5)
```

Full suites: `dart test` (Dart CI) and the bench-tests job cover both; the new tests embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (file byte-stable after exit; no record timestamped after exit).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain rounds ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — writers drop + warn once per class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settles after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal state, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel/timeout] --> K[kill fa: SIGTERM → SIGKILL → reap bounded]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

Second tier left as follow-up (per the ticket's tiering): SIGTERM graceful-seal path, tb-twin adapter (`bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`), and the standalone REG-1/REG-2 CI jobs — the invariants themselves are enforced and tested here.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). - adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. ### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).

# Changelog

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its

  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage

  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class

  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).

{"content":"### What changed

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). The headless `finally` and the REPL teardown seal as the LAST session action — same implementation, same close order: drain → usage fold → seal → exit (REG-2).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).
- Honest drains stay legal: assertions pin records to process exit, not the final-answer timestamp (E7/REG-1 guard).

### How to verify

```bash

python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v   # +6 AgentPhaseExitGuaranteeTest (AC4/AC7/IT-3/IT-5)
```

Full suites: `dart test` (Dart CI) and the bench-tests job cover both; the new tests embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (file byte-stable after exit; no record timestamped after exit).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain rounds ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — writers drop + warn once per class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settles after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal state, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel/timeout] --> K[kill fa: SIGTERM → SIGKILL → reap bounded]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

Second tier left as follow-up (per the ticket's tiering): SIGTERM graceful-seal path, tb-twin adapter (`bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`), and the standalone REG-1/REG-2 CI jobs — the invariants themselves are enforced and tested here.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(bench): gh-1643 — a trial killed mid-stream no longer reports 0/None
  usage. The fold read only FINALIZED assistant messages, so a run killed
  before its first assistant message (the costliest rows) folded to silent
  zeros. Both folds now price a dangling `model_request_summary` at its
  KNOWN request-side volume (system prompt + outbound message chars at the
  shared chars/4 rate, estimated input; output unknown) and mark the usage
  incomplete instead: `UsageChainScan.usageIncomplete` → `usage.json`
  (`usageIncomplete: true`, written only when set so completed folds stay
  byte-identical), `SessionUsage.usage_incomplete` → the tb adapter's
  `usage-guard.json` row and harbor's `agent_result.metadata`, and the
  post-mortem stamps `usage_incomplete` on every results.json row it
  patches from a partial fold. Harbor also exports the run outcome class
  (`agent_result.metadata.failure_mode`: agent_timeout self-kill /
  external_kill / completed / crashed / never_started) so downstream
  classification stops relying on exception.txt archaeology; a summary
  superseded by another summary is flushed instead of silently dropped on
  both sides. Never-started trials keep the gh-1638/gh-1576 audit-only
  precedence (no fake usage).
- fix(stuck-calls): gh-1632 — a stuck tool call in an interactive session now
  escalates like everywhere else. `effectiveStuckTool()` defaulted every
  non-headless host to `StuckFollowUpMode.advisory` when no explicit
  `agent.stuckTool:` was configured, so the fa 1.0.580 incident session (a
  dead `git fetch` in the REPL) fired its `tool_stuck` flag at the 300 s
  threshold and then hung for 27 more minutes — advisory mode never cancels,
  retries, or converts; only the owner's manual steering broke the deadlock.

  raises a fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) so a background-shell settle or
  task completion arriving after the final answer's drain — including the
  registry's one-turn-deferred listener racing `_finishHeadlessDrain`'s

The fence semantics: the run is exiting; new runs during the waiter stretch would extend the trial indefinitely (that's what gh-1455's abort path explicitly avoids). Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). - adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating.
