### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). - adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).
- Honest drains stay legal: assertions pin records to process exit, not the final-answer timestamp (E7/REG-1 guard).

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. {"content":"### What changed

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). The headless `finally` and the REPL teardown seal as the LAST session action — same implementation, same close order: drain → usage fold → seal → exit (REG-2).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).
- Honest drains stay legal: assertions pin records to process exit, not the final-answer timestamp (E7/REG-1 guard).

```bash

Full suites: `dart test` (Dart CI) and the bench-tests job cover both; the new tests embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (file byte-stable after exit; no record timestamped after exit).

  H[harbor cancel/timeout] --> K[kill fa: SIGTERM → SIGKILL → reap bounded]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). - Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). - adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).

Implements gh-1589's `SessionSeal` + agent-phase exit guarantee: a headless `fa -p` session JSONL becomes a sealed artifact — after the final answer's drain, the settle→reaction path is fenced and every session writer observes a closed file; and harbor's `run()` returns only after the fa process fully exited.

- fa (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`, `session_tree.dart`): `Session.seal()` — per-run writer state, no file-format change. Every append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped post-seal with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class; never throws (issue #413 exit-code semantics untouched). Resume opens the same file unsealed (I5).
- fa (CLI): the drain wrap-up raises a settle→reaction fence (`_reactionRunsSealed`) before its check-to-return window (E1) — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b 10:13:42–10:14:00 burst). The headless `finally` and the REPL teardown seal as the LAST session action — same implementation, same close order: drain → usage fold → seal → exit (REG-2).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): the ladder kill became terminate-and-reap (SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL escalation → pgrep confirm), and the external-cancel paths (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first — the incident's gap — plus the no-knobs exec and external-cap-only mode) now kill + reap before propagating. Reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced (AC7/E4).

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) for late writes — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- The seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration, `session_repair`/replay/registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry (not only in the `finally`) so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window; an in-flight reaction run is still awaited and lands inside the boundary (E3).

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. +    async def _kill_fa(self, environment, *, force: bool = False) -> bool:
+        """Best-effort SIGTERM (or SIGKILL with `force`) of the fa process.

+        Never raises — a failed kill is the escalation path's input, and
+        its failure must never replace the caller's own outcome (the

+    async def _fa_process_gone(self, environment, timeout: float) -> bool:
+        """Whether fa has exited, checked with ONE bounded server-side
+        poll loop (`pgrep` once a second for [timeout] seconds). A transport
+        error conservatively reports "alive" — the caller escalates.
+        """
+        try:

{"content":"### What changed

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. The headless drain wrap-up also raises a settle→reaction fence — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b post-answer burst).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): terminate-and-reap — the ladder kill and every external-cancel path (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first, no-knobs exec, external-cap-only) now SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm before returning; reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced.

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- Seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration; `session_repair`, replay, registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window (E1); an in-flight reaction run is still awaited inside the boundary (E3). One seal implementation for REPL-quit and headless (REG-2).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
```

The new ITs embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (no record timestamped after process exit; file byte-stable after exit — records between the final answer and the seal stay legal, E7). Second tier left as follow-up per the ticket's tiering: SIGTERM graceful-seal, tb-twin adapter, standalone REG CI jobs.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]

blocks.text:
### What changed

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. The headless drain wrap-up also raises a settle→reaction fence — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b post-answer burst).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): terminate-and-reap — the ladder kill and every external-cancel path (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first, no-knobs exec, external-cap-only) now SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm before returning; reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced.

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- Seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration; `session_repair`, replay, registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window (E1); an in-flight reaction run is still awaited inside the boundary (E3). One seal implementation for REPL-quit and headless (REG-2).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
```

The new ITs embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (no record timestamped after process exit; file byte-stable after exit — records between the final answer and the seal stay legal, E7). Left as follow-up per the ticket's tiering: SIGTERM graceful-seal, tb-twin adapter, standalone REG CI jobs, and the docker E2E legs.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — late writes dropped, 1 warning/class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settle after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel / timeout] --> K[SIGTERM → SIGKILL → bounded reap]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

### What changed

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. The headless drain wrap-up also raises a settle→reaction fence — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b post-answer burst).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): terminate-and-reap — the ladder kill and every external-cancel path (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first, no-knobs exec, external-cap-only) now SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm before returning; reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced.

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- Seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration; `session_repair`, replay, registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window (E1); an in-flight reaction run is still awaited inside the boundary (E3). One seal implementation for REPL-quit and headless (REG-2).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
```

The new ITs embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (no record timestamped after process exit; file byte-stable after exit — records between the final answer and the seal stay legal, E7). Left as follow-up per the ticket's tiering: SIGTERM graceful-seal, tb-twin adapter, standalone REG CI jobs, and the docker E2E legs.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — late writes dropped, 1 warning/class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settle after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel / timeout] --> K[SIGTERM → SIGKILL → bounded reap]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

### What changed

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. The headless drain wrap-up also raises a settle→reaction fence — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b post-answer burst).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): terminate-and-reap — the ladder kill and every external-cancel path (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first, no-knobs exec, external-cap-only) now SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm before returning; reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced.

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- Seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration; `session_repair`, replay, registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window (E1); an in-flight reaction run is still awaited inside the boundary (E3). One seal implementation for REPL-quit and headless (REG-2).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
```

The new ITs embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (no record timestamped after process exit; file byte-stable after exit — records between the final answer and the seal stay legal, E7). Left as follow-up per the ticket's tiering: SIGTERM graceful-seal, tb-twin adapter, standalone REG CI jobs, and the docker E2E legs.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — late writes dropped, 1 warning/class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settle after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel / timeout] --> K[SIGTERM → SIGKILL → bounded reap]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

### What changed

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. The headless drain wrap-up also raises a settle→reaction fence — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b post-answer burst).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): terminate-and-reap — the ladder kill and every external-cancel path (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first, no-knobs exec, external-cap-only) now SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm before returning; reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced.

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- Seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration; `session_repair`, replay, registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window (E1); an in-flight reaction run is still awaited inside the boundary (E3). One seal implementation for REPL-quit and headless (REG-2).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
```

The new ITs embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (no record timestamped after process exit; file byte-stable after exit — records between the final answer and the seal stay legal, E7).   H[harbor cancel / timeout] --> K[SIGTERM → SIGKILL → bounded reap]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

### What changed

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. The headless drain wrap-up also raises a settle→reaction fence — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b post-answer burst).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): terminate-and-reap — the ladder kill and every external-cancel path (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first, no-knobs exec, external-cap-only) now SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm before returning; reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced.

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- Seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration; `session_repair`, replay, registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window (E1); an in-flight reaction run is still awaited inside the boundary (E3). One seal implementation for REPL-quit and headless (REG-2).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
```

The new ITs embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (no record timestamped after process exit; file byte-stable after exit — records between the final answer and the seal stay legal, E7). Left as follow-up per the ticket's tiering: SIGTERM graceful-seal, tb-twin adapter, standalone REG CI jobs, and the docker E2E legs.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — late writes dropped, 1 warning/class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settle after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel / timeout] --> K[SIGTERM → SIGKILL → bounded reap]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

### What changed

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. The headless drain wrap-up also raises a settle→reaction fence — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b post-answer burst).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): terminate-and-reap — the ladder kill and every external-cancel path (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first, no-knobs exec, external-cap-only) now SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm before returning; reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced.

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- Seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration; `session_repair`, replay, registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window (E1); an in-flight reaction run is still awaited inside the boundary (E3). One seal implementation for REPL-quit and headless (REG-2).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
```

The new ITs embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (no record timestamped after process exit; file byte-stable after exit — records between the final answer and the seal stay legal, E7). Left as follow-up per the ticket's tiering: SIGTERM graceful-seal, tb-twin adapter, standalone REG CI jobs, and the docker E2E legs.

  J[job settle after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel / timeout] --> K[SIGTERM → SIGKILL → bounded reap]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

### What changed

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. The headless drain wrap-up also raises a settle→reaction fence — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b post-answer burst).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): terminate-and-reap — the ladder kill and every external-cancel path (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first, no-knobs exec, external-cap-only) now SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm before returning; reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced.

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- Seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration; `session_repair`, replay, registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window (E1); an in-flight reaction run is still awaited inside the boundary (E3). One seal implementation for REPL-quit and headless (REG-2).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
```

The new ITs embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (no record timestamped after process exit; file byte-stable after exit — records between the final answer and the seal stay legal, E7). Left as follow-up per the ticket's tiering: SIGTERM graceful-seal, tb-twin adapter, standalone REG CI jobs, and the docker E2E legs.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[final answer] --> D[drain ≤ headless.shellJobDrainMs]
  D --> F[_finishHeadlessDrain: reaction fence ON]
  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — late writes dropped, 1 warning/class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settle after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel / timeout] --> K[SIGTERM → SIGKILL → bounded reap]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>

### What changed

- fa: new `Session.seal()` (`lib/src/session_seal.dart`) — after `runHeadless` completes (any terminal stop reason) and in the REPL teardown, the session writer seals: every late append (`_persistMessages`, `shell_job_registry`, compaction, any `appendCustomEntry`, leaf moves) is dropped with exactly ONE stderr warning per writer class, never thrown. The headless drain wrap-up also raises a settle→reaction fence — a shell-job/task settle after the final answer's drain does board bookkeeping only: no `_startRun`, no model request, no record (kills the 65gGW7b post-answer burst).
- adapter (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`): terminate-and-reap — the ladder kill and every external-cancel path (harbor's own `wait_for` firing first, no-knobs exec, external-cap-only) now SIGTERM → bounded exec await → SIGKILL → pgrep confirm before returning; reap timeout ⇒ loud `agent-phase exit guarantee degraded` note, deadline still enforced.

### Key decisions

- Drop + warn (not hard-fail) — the exit code stays the turn's terminal outcome (ticket open question, recommended option).
- Seal is per-run state in the writer, not a file marker — no migration; `session_repair`, replay, registry recovery unchanged (AC5/AC6 by construction).
- Fence raised at `_finishHeadlessDrain` entry so the deferred settle listener can't slip through the wrap-up window (E1); an in-flight reaction run is still awaited inside the boundary (E3). One seal implementation for REPL-quit and headless (REG-2).

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/session_seal_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_seal_test.dart
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
```

The new ITs embed the REG-1 watchdog assertions (no record timestamped after process exit; file byte-stable after exit — records between the final answer and the seal stay legal, E7). Left as follow-up per the ticket's tiering: SIGTERM graceful-seal, tb-twin adapter, standalone REG CI jobs, and the docker E2E legs.

```mermaid

  F --> U[usage fold + board/obligations/subagent flush]
  U --> S[Session.seal — late writes dropped, 1 warning/class]
  S --> X[exit]
  J[job settle after wrap-up] -->|bookkeeping only| B[board terminal, no _startRun]
  H[harbor cancel / timeout] --> K[SIGTERM → SIGKILL → bounded reap]
  K --> R[run returns only after fa exited]
```

</details>
